text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.5% today after falling sharply on November 23rd, bouncing back as oil prices stabilized and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East spiked. Iran's report of tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and ongoing Houthi threats to Saudi oil infrastructure created supply-risk concerns that supported crude prices—US oil holding near $89.50 per barrel helps the company's production economics and cash flow.

The rebound also reflects a pullback from the worst of last week's sell-off, which was triggered by the failed climate negotiations (which spooked investors worried about fossil fuel regulation) and a broader cooling of the refinery-profit trade that had driven energy stocks higher. While refinery margins are unwinding, the geopolitical premium in oil prices is now working in an upstream producer's favor.
